name: Musée Théodore Monod d'Art Africain (IFAN)
watch: The museum's own partners page lists Fondation TOTAL Sénégal among current partners. TotalEnergies is an excluded funder under active campaign. Other partners: Fondation SOCOCIM (cement), Gerda Henkel, Volkswagen Foundation, the French Embassy, Goethe-Institut and Grand Palais RMN.
why_flagged: The museum's own partners page lists Fondation TOTAL Sénégal among current partners. TotalEnergies is an excluded funder under active campaign. Other partners: Fondation SOCOCIM (cement), Gerda Henkel, Volkswagen Foundation, the French Embassy, Goethe-Institut and Grand Palais RMN.
records_note: The museum sits inside IFAN at Cheikh Anta Diop University and posts no reports, accounts, donors or board of its own.

name: Museo Amparo
funding: Fundación Amparo, set up by banker Manuel Espinosa Yglesias, funds the museum.
watch: Name to know: FEMSA. Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas marched in April 2017 to cancel Coca-Cola FEMSA's water concession.
why_flagged: Name to know: FEMSA. Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas marched in April 2017 to cancel Coca-Cola FEMSA's water concession.
records_note: Owner Fundación Amparo posts a 2025 activities report; neither site shows accounts, donors or a board, only a staff directory.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Caracas
funding: Venezuelan public museum, under the state's Fundación Museos Nacionales since 2005, with the Ministry of Culture overseeing it.
watch: Chávez dismissed founder Sofía Ímber on air in January 2001. A January 2006 Culture Ministry notice dropped her name from the museum.
why_flagged: Venezuelan public museum, under the state's Fundación Museos Nacionales since 2005, with the Ministry of Culture overseeing it. No private sponsor found.
records_note: The museum's site and its parent foundation's site did not load, so its records are unchecked.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Panamá
funding: Private non-profit funded by companies and art lovers. Naturgy, a gas and electricity group, signed a sponsorship in April 2023 covering upkeep and operations.
watch: Naturgy is a gas utility group; its Panama arm distributes electricity. Donor logos on the museum's site carry no names.
why_flagged: Private non-profit funded by companies and art lovers. Naturgy, a gas and electricity group, signed a sponsorship in April 2023 covering upkeep and operations.
records_note: Publishes annual reports for 2018 to 2025 and a named board; donor logos carry no names or date, and no financial statements are posted.

name: Museo de Arte de Lima
funding: 2023: half from courses, a quarter Patronato members, a quarter events/tickets; about 150k visits; allies Fundación Telefónica, ICPNA.
watch: Camisea, operated by Pluspetrol, sponsored free Thursday entry from August 2022 to March 2025. Alberto Rebaza chairs the board.
why_flagged: KPMG-audited 2025 revenue S/17.1M: tuition 38%, donations and memberships 37%, services 25%. Donors named: Fundación Telefónica, JOMA, THOMA, Smurfit Kappa. Camisea gas consortium funded free Thursdays.
records_note: Posts audited accounts for 2003 to 2025, committee annual reports for 2007 to 2021 and a named board; its partners page shows an unnamed banner.

name: Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico
funding: Private nonprofit. Current exhibitions are backed by the Flamboyan Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Mano Amiga and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company.
watch: On 19 November 2023 activists picketed after the Cecilia Orta Allende gallery was renamed for a donor family tied to the Fiscal Oversight Board.
why_flagged: Private nonprofit. Current exhibitions are backed by the Flamboyan Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Mano Amiga and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company. No corporate donors are named.
records_note: Its site names 19 board members but posts no annual report, accounts or donor list; Form 990s for 2000 to 2025 are on ProPublica.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá
watch: Fundación BAT (British American Tobacco Colombia) is a 2025 gala private donor; March 2026 row over curator Eugenio Viola's dismissal, nepotism and labour claims (170 signatories).
why_flagged: Fundación BAT (British American Tobacco Colombia) is a 2025 gala private donor; March 2026 row over curator Eugenio Viola's dismissal, nepotism and labour claims (170 signatories).
records_note: MAMBO publishes no annual report, accounts or board; its gala page shows sponsor logos grouped by year, 2023 to 2025.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires
watch: TotalEnergies and Samsung on supporter list.
why_flagged: TotalEnergies and Samsung on supporter list.
records_note: Posts management reports for 2021 and 2022 and shows supporter logos with no names or date; accounts and any board are not published.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Santo Domingo
funding: State museum run by the Dominican Ministry of Culture on the Plaza de la Cultura; its director sits on the ministry's Bienal Nacional commission.
watch: After a December 2019 protest, artists' open letters in 2020 and 2021 blamed the ministry, the museum and its directors for the Bienal's delays.
why_flagged: State museum run by the Dominican Ministry of Culture on the Plaza de la Cultura; its director sits on the ministry's Bienal Nacional commission.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; its parent Ministry of Culture posts annual memorias for 2016 to 2025 and financial statements for 2020 to 2025.

name: Museo de la Solidaridad Salvador Allende
funding: Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural grant of CLP 660M in 2025. Project money from Fondart, the Senate, Henry Moore Foundation and Centro Cultural de España. Metro is a media partner.
watch: In 2023 Allende's grandson wrote to the museum, then campaigned publicly, demanding Tania Bruguera's show be cancelled. It opened late and modified.
why_flagged: Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural grant of CLP 660M in 2025. Project money from Fondart, the Senate, Henry Moore Foundation and Centro Cultural de España. Metro is a media partner.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2014 to 2025, balances, a 2025 list of funders and agreements, and five named directors.

name: Museo Jumex
funding: Fundación Jumex runs the museum with no board, funded by profits of the Grupo Jumex juice company. Admission is free.
watch: Free museum in Mexico City's Polanco district. Its operating budget comes from the Grupo Jumex beverage conglomerate, under family foundation governance.
why_flagged: Fundación Jumex runs the museum with no board, funded by profits of the Grupo Jumex juice company. Admission is free.
records_note: The museum's foundation posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; the site names only Grupo Jumex as the source of support.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia
funding: Run since 2003 by the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a state foundation.
watch: In June 2020 the foundation's new board forced out director Max Hinderer Cruz; CIMAM urged it to withdraw the request.
why_flagged: Run since 2003 by the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a state foundation. No outside sponsor is named; donated artworks arrive through the Foreign Ministry.
records_note: The museum's parent foundation posts reports for 2019 to 2025, financial statements for 2018 to 2025 and its council, but no sponsor list.
